gen-metal-mania-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Heavy, intense, a little menacing: Metal Mania hits with dense lettering and big open eyes on every e. Be Vietnam Pro sits beneath it, cool and clean, its curve endings held well apart.
gen-metal-mania-fs-karma: Trustworthy and classic, the text here reads with a mellow modulation that never snags the eye. Karma holds steady under Metal Mania, whose single-width strokes feel heavy and intense.
gen-modak-fs-erode: Fun and approachable, Modak draws every stroke at a single width, with lowercase eyes as big as washers. Erode brings the editorial dignity, its serif curves thinning gently where they turn.
gen-nixie-one-gf-actor: Nostalgic, retro-tech, thread-thin: that is Nixie One. Actor adds clean, modern letters with wide s curves barely curled in, a tidy, easygoing partner to the heading's constant, unpressured line.
gen-nixie-one-zilla-slab: Nostalgic and retro-tech, Nixie One draws a steady line with no pressure variation from top to baseline. Zilla Slab, a sturdy, technical slab-serif, gives it a firm footing underneath.
gen-syne-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab is grounded, refined, and tall in every lowercase letter. Syne is best at commanding, experimental display, all bent-wire strokes, while the text serif quietly handles the refined reading.
gen-syne-fs-erode: Wiry, commanding, and unpinched: that is Syne. It does experimental display best, with no pressure swells at all, while Erode does editorial dignity best, its stroke weight ebbing gently.
gen-tourney-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Wide-tracked and athletic, Tourney cuts every stroke to one width. Mochiy Pop One runs text with very large lowercase eyes, letters hung like clothespins on a line, giving a neutral, professional feel.
gen-ultra-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and vintage, Ultra packs its letters close with only a slight swell in each bowl. But Bespoke Sans, sharp and refined, leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, so text reads freely.
gen-unbounded-fs-gambetta: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide, with a welcoming c. That heading does friendly, contemporary display best, while Gambetta does bookish grace best, its stroke weight shifting noticeably but never dramatically.
